newsitem.title: UK: London stocks fall on rate rise, Nikkei drops.
newsitem.headline: London stocks fall on rate rise, Nikkei drops.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - Leading shares finished sharply lower after an interest rate rise surprised the market, which had predicted no change in rates ahead of a general election. The FTSE 100 closed down 29.6 points at 3,963.9, falling through key chart support levels on the way.

FRANKFURT- German shares ended bourse trade slightly higher, but at the day's low point, after the dollar slipped and German bonds lost some sheen following the surprise raising of British interest rates. The DAX index of 30 blue-chip shares closed up 5.11 points, or 0.19 percent, at 2,678.73. In post-bourse trade the index fell 10.78 to 2,664.72.

PARIS - French stocks faded at session end to close slightly lower as questions about the direction of interest rates in Europe weighed on markets. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 0.98 points or 0.05 percent at 2,124.76.

ZURICH - Swiss shares dropped in the second half of the session to close near the day's lows when investors turned cautious after watching the market spend most of the day in positive terrain. The all-share Swiss Performance Index fell 4.49 points, or 0.19 percent, to close at 2,391.32 points.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks finished sharply lower, battered by news that a regional bank had said it suspects a former employee misused bank funds. Futures-linked selling also depressed the market. The key Nikkei 225 average tumbled 276.41 points to 20,681.67.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed sharply higher after staging a strong rally prompted by the upturn in U.S. markets overnight and the expiry of October Hang Seng index futures, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index closed 213.30 points higher at 12,405.47.

SYDNEY - Australian shares finished up and near their highs after the influential bank sector benefited from a bond market rally following a surge in U.S. Treasuries on Tuesday. The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index closed 13.7 points higher at 2,336.7.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended the day on a firmer footing as institutions seeking bargains entered the market in late trade. Golds ended a touch stronger after hovering in negative territory for most of the day. The overall index ended up 23.8 points 6,891.8 points, the industrial index gained 10.3 points to 8,124.7 points and the gold index was up 2.1 points to 1,708.1 points.
